scenes.title: The Clock Tower Key
scenes.card: Nell the clock keeper leaves her key on a rock by the stream. The village clock stops, Nell searches in despair, and a little girl who found the key brings it home.

scenes.title: The key is left behind
scenes.card: Nell sets her tower key on a flat rock to wash her hands, hears the bell and hurries away without it.

subtitles.text: Nell: Eight o’clock sharp. The whole village sets its day by my clock.
Nell: Cold stream water first. A clock keeper needs clean hands.
Nell: That was the quarter bell already? Oh, I am late!

scenes.title: The clock stops
scenes.card: The clock stops. Nell has lost her key and sets off to look at the stream.

subtitles.text: Nell: Granny Ada, the clock has stopped! It still says half past six.
Granny Ada: It is nearly nine, Nell. Did you wind it this morning?
Nell: I was about to... oh no. My key is not on my belt.
Pol: Where did you last have it?
Nell: At the stream. I set it on the flat rock while I washed my hands.
Pol: Then the rock is where we start. Go, we will keep the village calm.
Nell: Thank you, both. I will be quick!

scenes.title: Mina finds the key
scenes.card: Mina finds the golden key on the rock. Joss knows it belongs to the clock tower.

subtitles.text: Mina: A golden key, lying on the flat rock. Maybe it opens a treasure chest!
Farmer Joss: Mina! That is no toy. That is the key to the clock tower.
Mina: The clock stopped this morning. Somebody must be so worried!
Farmer Joss: We will take it back together.
Mina: I will carry it. I found it!

scenes.title: The key comes home
scenes.card: Mina returns the key. Nell winds the clock and the bell rings.

subtitles.text: Mina: Miss Nell? Is this what you are looking for? It was on the flat rock.
Nell: My key! Mina, you wonderful girl. I thought the whole village was lost to time.
Farmer Joss: She would not let me carry it once.
Pol: An honest soul picked it up. We have a few of those.
Granny Ada: Or a magpie. They do love anything shiny.
Nell: Stand back, everyone. Time to wake up the clock.
Pol: Right on time. My bread thanks you, Nell!

scenes.title: A bun for a hero
scenes.card: The villagers share a bun and laugh. The clock keeps perfect time.

subtitles.text: Pol: This one is for you, Mina. Still warm from the oven.
Mina: For me? It smells like cinnamon. Thank you, Pol!
Farmer Joss: Not a bad morning, Pol. Mina found a key, and I found an excuse for a second breakfast.
Pol: And I found a reason to bake a bigger batch tomorrow.
Granny Ada: Noon on the dot, Nell. It was almost worth the fright.
Nell: Never again. Tonight I tie that key to my belt with a double knot.
